text:
tam: noticed a spike of half-open streaming connections yesterday where upstream would stall after initial tokens and we accumulated many 499s. thinking we need an edge-side adaptive cutoff instead of letting streams sit.
viv: can you share a minimal repro or trace? which routes were affected?
tam: trace: https://s.re/r/trace/def456 - mostly chat-stream routes to model-family-x, upstream p95 ~3.5s for ~45s window.
sam: high level approach: 1) define 'first-token window' (e.g., 300ms). 2) if upstream emits no tokens in window, edge returns a deterministic truncated frame with header X-Edge-Cutoff:1 OR launches a hedged local inference to a cheaper variant. route opt-in only.
viv: semantics are tricky. clients expect streaming tokens; we need SDK changes to surface 'truncated' and keep backwards compatibility. Also disallow for endpoints with side effects.
eloise: infra-bot: alert: ingress.open_streams > baseline*2 in eu-west-1 for 00:45 - linked incident 6321
tam: what about observability triggers? propose composite trigger = upstream_first_token_p50 > threshold OR ingress_queue_ratio > 2, plus per-tenant leaky-bucket to prevent flapping.
sam: metrics to add: edge.cutoff.count, edge.cutoff.reason, edge.hedge.count, trace tag edge.cutoff=true. include route.tolerance_ms in span.
viv: billing: if we short-circuit before upstream consumes tokens, bill only consumed tokens and label reason=edge_cutoff. if we hedged, bill both but mark primary_failed. need billing RFC.
tam: rollout plan: truncate-only canary on internal dev routes at 0.5% for 1 week. monitor 499 rate, p50 latency, and eval set quality. if stable, ramp and consider hedging A/B.
everyone: agree to owners? sam -> edge impl + PR, viv -> SDK + billing mapping, tam -> rollout + canary config, eloise -> runbook and alerts.
infra-bot: reminder scheduled: follow-up review in 12 days.
